facts.statement: Iberotrygon lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
The genus is known from a holotype antero-lateral tooth and several paratype teeth, including four from a single juvenile and one isolated tooth.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype MPZ 2005-33, an antero-lateral tooth, and the parartypes MPZ 2005-34, four well-preserved teeth from a single juvenile?, and MPZ 2005-35, an isolated tooth

facts.statement: Only one species, Iberotrygon plagiolophus, is known, and it was named and described in 2009.
facts.quote: Only the single species I. plagiolophus, is known; it was named and described in 2009.

facts.statement: The tooth crown features a well-developed, high, pointed main cusp that inclines lingually in both juvenile and adult teeth.
facts.quote: The tooth crown of Iberotrygon is cuspidate, with a well-developed, high, pointed, main cusp that is inclined lingually in teeth of juveniles and adults.

facts.statement: The lingual margin of the tooth crown overhangs the root, particularly near the apex.
facts.quote: The lingual margin of the crown overhangs the root, especially towards the apex.

facts.statement: In occlusal view, the crown lacks distinct transversal crests.
facts.quote: In occlusal view the crown is devoid of distinct transversal crests.

facts.statement: The crown features ornamentation including a longitudinal medio-labial ridge that sometimes bifurcates at the base to delimit the apron.
facts.quote: However, there is some ornamentation, most notably a longitudinal medio-labial ridge, which sometimes bifurcates basally delimiting the apron.

facts.statement: Conspicuous short vertical ridges are present at the base of the labial crown.
facts.quote: There are conspicuous short vertical ridges at the labial crown base.

facts.statement: The lingual face is steep and features a well-developed vertical uvula above a well-marked central depression.
facts.quote: The lingual face is fairly steep, and has a well-developed vertical directed uvula, above which is a well-marked central depression.

facts.statement: Teeth of Iberotrygon show ontogenetic variation, differing between juvenile and adult stages.
facts.quote: Teeth of Iberotrygon display some sort of ontogenetic variation.

facts.statement: Iberotrygon teeth resemble those of Ptychotrygon, Texatrygon, and Archingeayia but can be easily distinguished by a specific combination of characters.
facts.quote: Teeth of Iberotrygon resemble those of Ptychotrygon, Texatrygon and Archingeayia to some extent but can easily be distinguished from those by the character combination indicated in the diagnosis.

facts.statement: The genus Iberotrygon was established by Kriwet, Nunn, and Klug in 2009.
The species Iberotrygon plagiolophus was named by Kriwet, Nunn, and Klug in 2009.
Iberotrygon belongs to the parent group Sclerorhynchiformes.
